competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K Business section as a core design principle of the platform
competitive_position.claim: Millrose differentiates itself from traditional land banking through a self-funding capital recycling model in which takedown proceeds are continuously redeployed into new land acquisitions without re-initiating external capital raising.
quotes: Unlike private-market, traditional land bank solutions, we continuously recycle our capital to fund land acquisition and development for our counterparties on a consistent basis, rather than returning takedown proceeds to our external investors and re-initiating the capital raising process.

This perpetual self-funding recurring process provides us with the ability to generate cash that is then recycled back into future properties, even during periods of market downturn or periods of depressed market conditions.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K Risk Factors section
competitive_position.claim: Millrose's competitive position is threatened by its continued reliance on Lennar as its largest counterparty, with Lennar holding exclusive Founder's Rights including Enforcement Rights that allow it to compel sales and stop all monthly option payments on all properties if Millrose refuses to sell.
quotes: Lennar is currently our largest counterparty and our business was initially formed to engage in land bank transactions with Lennar as well as potential Lennar Related Ventures and Other Counterparties.

If we refuse to sell homesites to Lennar after it exercises a purchase option, Lennar has an Enforcement Right by which it can compel us to sell and, if we fail to comply within a ten-day cure period, Lennar may immediately stop all monthly option payments on all properties covered by the Lennar Agreements without penalty or breach.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K Risk Factors section
competitive_position.claim: Millrose's recycled capital business model is contingent on counterparties electing to exercise their land purchase options; they are under no obligation to do so and may decline in a significant market downturn, forcing Millrose to bear the cost of construction and resale to third parties.
quotes: our counterparties are under no obligation to exercise their land purchase options and purchase the homesites, and they may decline to exercise them in the event of a significant downturn in the market.
The price for which we can sell homes to third parties may be significantly less than the amounts of our investments.

quotes: Our Real Estate Portfolio is concentrated in three states (California, Florida and Texas), with a substantial portion located in Florida and Texas.
Approximately 50% of the property assets are concentrated in three states (California, Florida, Texas) and approximately 41% are located in two strong housing market states: Florida and Texas

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K Risk Factors section
competitive_position.claim: Millrose's ability to obtain additional debt financing is constrained by a Debt-to-Equity Ratio Limit requiring Lennar's prior approval if the combined ratio exceeds 1:1, which may restrict its ability to fund growth or provide capital to counterparties.
quotes: Under the Lennar Agreements, Millrose may not enter into third-party financing arrangements that would cause the combined debt-to-equity ratio of Millrose and its affiliates to exceed 1:1 without Lennar's prior approval.

Lennar's Capital Priority Right limits the amount of capital Millrose has available for transactions with counterparties other than Lennar or Lennar Related Ventures, which may make it difficult to provide our homesite option platform to such counterparties.

material_events.claim: Millrose issued $750 million aggregate principal amount of 6.25% senior notes due 2032, using proceeds to repay the remaining $500 million DDTL Credit Facility balance.
quotes: On September 11, 2025, we issued $750 million aggregate principal amount of 6.25% senior notes due 2032, using the net proceeds therefrom to repay the entire $500 million remaining principal amount outstanding under the DDTL Credit Facility, and related expenses.

material_events.claim: Lennar completed an Exchange Offer, exchanging 33,298,754 shares of Millrose Class A Common Stock for 8,049,594 shares of Lennar Class A common stock, leaving Lennar with a de minimis stake.
quotes: On November 26, 2025, Lennar announced the results of the Exchange Offer through which Lennar accepted an aggregate of 8,049,594 shares of Lennar Class A common stock in exchange for 33,298,754 shares of Class A Common Stock of Millrose. The Exchange Offer was completed on November 28, 2025.

material_events.claim: Millrose entered into a new Credit Agreement providing a $1.335 billion four-year Revolving Credit Facility, a $500 million DDTL Credit Facility, and an accordion feature up to $2.5 billion aggregate.
quotes: On March 25, 2026, the Company entered into the Credit Agreement (as defined below) that provides for (i) a four-year Revolving Credit Facility (as defined below) with commitments in an aggregate amount of $1.335 billion, (ii) a DDTL Credit Facility (as defined below) in an aggregate amount of $500 million that may be utilized during the first year following the Effective Date (as defined below), and (iii) an uncommitted accordion feature that allows the Company to seek additional loan commitments under the Credit Agreement in the future, subject to an aggregate maximum commitment amount of $2.5 billion.

material_events.claim: Millrose amended its Credit Agreement (Amendment No. 1) to reduce the loan interest rate by 0.25% per annum.
quotes: On August 5, 2026, the Company entered into Amendment No. 1 to the Credit Agreement. The Credit Agreement was amended pursuant to Amendment No.1 to, among other things, reduce the rate at which the loans bear interest by 0.25% per annum.

material_events.claim: Millrose exercised the accordion feature to increase its Revolving Credit Facility by $50 million to $1.385 billion.
quotes: On September 21, 2026, the Company and the guarantors entered into the Commitment and Acceptance, by and among the Company, the guarantors, JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., as administrative agent for the lenders, and Flagstar Bank, N.A., under which the Company exercised the accordion feature under the Credit Agreement to increase the aggregate amount of commitments of the Revolving Credit Facility by $50 million to $1.385 billion.

material_events.claim: Millrose provided approximately $1.068 billion in total capital support for Dream Finders' acquisition of Beazer Homes, including a $170.6 million preferred instrument in Q3 2026 and a subsequent $896.9 million (comprising a $316.9 million preferred instrument net of OID and $580.0 million in homesite acquisitions).
quotes: During the third quarter of 2026, the Company provided acquisition funding of $170.6 million to support Dream Finders' acquisition of Beazer Homes USA, Inc. (“Beazer Homes”).

Subsequent to the third quarter of 2026, upon the completion of Dream Finders' acquisition of Beazer Homes, the Company provided an additional $896.9 million funding through the purchase of a preferred instrument issued by Dream Finders for $316.9 million, net of original issue discount, and through the acquisition of homesites subject to option agreements with Dream Finders for $580.0 million. Total funding provided by the Company to Dream Finders was approximately $1.068 billion.
Subsequent to Quarter End, Completed $1.1 Billion of Capital Support in Connection with Dream Finders Homes’ Acquisition of Beazer Homes

material_events.claim: Millrose closed its first multifamily land banking partnership with JPI (a subsidiary of Sumitomo Forestry Co., Ltd.) and Kennedy Lewis Investment Management.
quotes: On July 30, 2026, the Company announced the closing of the first acquisition in a new land banking facility established by JPI, a premier developer of multifamily communities and subsidiary of Sumitomo Forestry Co., Ltd., and Kennedy Lewis Investment Management, to fund Class A multifamily land acquisition and development across JPI’s target markets.

material_events.claim: Millrose acquired 1,233 single-family residential properties from Lennar for approximately $333 million during Q3 2026, financed with ~$213 million under the SFR Secured Credit Facility and cash.
quotes: During the third quarter of 2026, the Company acquired 1,233 single-family residential properties from Lennar for approximately $333 million, inclusive of acquisition costs and capitalized property costs, which was financed with borrowings of approximately $213 million under our SFR Secured Credit Facility and cash on hand.

material_events.claim: Millrose entered into the SFR Secured Credit Facility with commitments up to $235.0 million (expandable to $1.0 billion), with $213.1 million outstanding as of September 30, 2026.
quotes: On September 30, 2026, certain subsidiaries of the Company entered into the SFR Secured Credit Facility. The SFR Secured Credit Facility provides for a revolving credit facility with commitments in an aggregate amount of up to $235.0 million. Lenders may agree to (a) increase the aggregate commitments up to $1.0 billion, or (b) make advances in excess of the committed amount but not to exceed a total outstanding balance of $1.0 billion. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had $213.1 million of outstanding borrowings under the SFR Secured Credit Facility.

material_events.claim: Millrose completed a $1.0 billion private offering of senior notes: $500.0 million of 6.500% notes due 2029 and $500.0 million of 6.750% notes due 2031.
quotes: On October 6, 2026, Millrose Properties, Inc. (“Millrose” or the “Company”) completed the offer and sale (the “Offering”) of $1.0 billion aggregate principal amount of senior notes in two separate tranches, one consisting of $500.0 million aggregate principal amount of 6.500% senior notes due 2029 (the “2029 Notes”) and the other consisting of $500.0 million aggregate principal amount of 6.750% senior notes due 2031 (the “2031 Notes” and, together with the 2029 Notes, the “Notes”).

material_events.claim: Millrose's Board of Directors authorized a new $250 million share repurchase program for its Class A common stock.
quotes: On October 26, 2026, the Company's Board of Directors authorized a new $250 million share repurchase program of the Company’s Class A common stock, par value $0.01 per share.

material_events.claim: Millrose raised its fourth quarter 2026 AFFO outlook to $0.82 to $0.84 per share, following a record Q3 AFFO of $0.80 per share (the sixth consecutive quarterly AFFO increase).
quotes: Third Quarter AFFO of $0.80 Per Share, the Sixth Consecutive Quarterly AFFO Increase; Raises Fourth Quarter AFFO Outlook to $0.82 to $0.84 Per Share
Raising guidance for year-end 2026 Adjusted Funds from Operations (AFFO) quarterly run rate to a range of $0.82 to $0.84 per share.

material_events.claim: Millrose declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.79 per share (approximately $131.2 million), paid on October 15, 2026.
quotes: On September 23, 2026, the Company’s Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.79 per share on the Company’s Class A common stock and Class B common stock, payable on October 15, 2026, to stockholders of record as of the close of business on October 5, 2026.

material_events.claim: Millrose entered into agreements with Lennar to acquire 620 additional single-family residential properties for approximately $150.3 million, with an expected net investment of approximately $50 million after anticipated asset-level limited recourse financing.
quotes: The Company has entered into agreements with Lennar to acquire 620 additional single-family residential properties for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $150.3 million, with an expected net investment of approximately $50 million after anticipated asset-level limited recourse financing.

risks.basis: stated in P6 (earnings release) and P2 (10-K risk factors); the 42% figure is a management statement in the CEO quote
risks.claim: Approximately 58% of Millrose's asset base remains invested under the Lennar Master Program Agreement, creating heavy counterparty concentration despite diversification efforts.
quotes: With the completion of the Dream Finders financing, approximately 42% of our asset base is now invested outside the Lennar Master Program Agreement

Lennar is currently our largest counterparty and our business was initially formed to engage in land bank transactions with Lennar as well as potential Lennar Related Ventures and Other Counterparties.

risks.basis: stated in P2 (10-K risk factors), Item 1A
risks.claim: The recycled-capital business model depends on counterparties electing to exercise their land purchase options; in a significant housing downturn, counterparties may decline to exercise, halting capital recycling.
quotes: The continued sustainability of Millrose's recycled capital business model, which is intended to generally provide Millrose with reliable, consistent and uninterrupted access to capital, is contingent on our counterparties electing to exercise their land purchase options.

our counterparties are under no obligation to exercise their land purchase options and purchase the homesites, and they may decline to exercise them in the event of a significant downturn in the market.

risks.basis: stated in P3 (10-K MD&A, Properties section) and P2 (10-K risk factors)
risks.claim: Roughly 50% of Millrose's property assets are concentrated in California, Florida, and Texas, with about 41% in Florida and Texas alone, exposing the portfolio to regional market and environmental shocks.
quotes: Approximately 50% of the property assets are concentrated in three states (California, Florida, Texas) and approximately 41% are located in two strong housing market states: Florida and Texas

Our Real Estate Portfolio is concentrated in three states (California, Florida and Texas), with a substantial portion located in Florida and Texas. This geographic concentration may increase our exposure to market fluctuations and environmental risks

risks.basis: stated in P2 (10-K risk factors); the $9,902,361 figure is from F1 balance sheet (table in thousands)
risks.claim: Millrose has not obtained independent appraisals or valuations for its real estate assets, including those acquired in the Spin-Off and the Rausch Transaction, so the carrying values on the balance sheet lack third-party validation.
quotes: We have not obtained independent appraisals or valuations for our real estate assets, including the assets acquired in the Spin-Off and the Rausch Transaction.
As a result, we cannot assure you that the values assigned to our real estate assets are accurate.

risks.basis: stated in P2 (10-K risk factors), under the heading 'Any exercise by Lennar of its Enforcement Rights...'
risks.claim: Lennar's Enforcement Rights allow it to compel Millrose to sell homesites and, upon non-compliance within ten days, to stop all monthly option payments on all Lennar-covered properties without penalty, creating severe cash-flow pressure.
quotes: If we refuse to sell homesites to Lennar after it exercises a purchase option, Lennar has an Enforcement Right by which it can compel us to sell and, if we fail to comply within a ten-day cure period, Lennar may immediately stop all monthly option payments on all properties covered by the Lennar Agreements without penalty or breach.
This could significantly reduce our cash flow and jeopardize our ability to maintain working capital and make required distributions to qualify as a REIT.

risks.basis: stated in P2 (10-K risk factors); the 42% and 22-counterparty figures are from P6
risks.claim: If Lennar or another major counterparty enters bankruptcy, the Master Program Agreement and Master Option Agreement may become unenforceable, potentially eliminating Millrose's primary revenue source.
quotes: If we or any of our major counterparties, including Lennar, enter into bankruptcy, key agreements such as the Master Program Agreement or the Master Option Agreement may become unenforceable.

Given the significance of our agreements with Lennar to our operations, if Lennar entered into bankruptcy it would likely have a severe adverse impact on our business and could force us into bankruptcy unless we are able to quickly establish relationships with other Lennar Related Ventures or additional counterparties.

risks.basis: F1 balance sheet (table in thousands); P2 risk factors; P1 10-K Business section for the 1:1 ratio; P4 MD&A for the accordion and SFR facility; P6 for the $0.8 billion takedown proceeds and $250 million repurchase
risks.claim: Millrose carries $3,127,456 (table in thousands) of debt obligations plus $210,596 (table in thousands) under the SFR Secured Credit Facility, with a contractual 1:1 debt-to-equity ceiling under the Lennar Agreements that constrains additional borrowing.
quotes: our ability to obtain additional debt financing is subject to the Debt-to-Equity Ratio Limit, which may restrict the level of financing we can obtain.
Millrose may not enter into third-party financing arrangements that would cause the combined debt-to-equity ratio of Millrose and its affiliates to exceed 1:1 without Lennar's prior approval.

The financial information included in this Form 10-K for the periods prior to the Spin-Off do not reflect the financial condition, results of operations or cash flows that we probably would have achieved as a separate, publicly-traded company during the pre-Spin-Off periods
